title: Striking individual differences in color perception uncovered by 'the dress' photograph
authors: Rosa Lafer-Sousa, Katherine L. Hermann, Bevil R. Conway
key_findings: Free-response survey N=1401 (313 naive): 57% blue/black, 30% white/gold, 11% blue/brown, 2% other.
Women and older people reported white/gold more; some observers switched on re-test (multistable); colour matches showed three peaks = three stable percepts.
Hypothesis: different priors about the illuminant along the daylight locus (cool prior -> white/gold, warm prior -> blue/black, neutral -> blue/brown).

Embedding the dress in scenes with a global warm or cool tint (including the model's skin) flipped most observers: 64% of W/G switched to B/K under warm light, 80% of B/K switched to W/G under cool light.
Larger image size increased W/G reports; blurring decreased them; chronotype trend not significant.
practical_applications: Product colours on the blue-yellow axis (navy, tortoise, brown/blue tints) need unambiguous illumination cues.
A tint applied to the whole scene incl. skin is read as light; check images at thumbnail size.
limitations: Short correspondence + supplement; online sample mostly US; mechanism partly hypothetical.

title: Color Perception: Objects, Constancy, and Categories
key_findings: Natural objects have polychromatic colour distributions; observers estimate object lightness from the brightest parts excluding highlights.
Chromatic and luminance contrast are statistically independent in natural scenes; chroma tends to mark objects while luminance also varies with shading.
Memory colour effect: colour-diagnostic objects (e.g. a grey banana) look tinted toward their typical colour; strongest along blue-yellow; observers most uncertain along the daylight axis.

Constancy indices across 30 years range from near zero to near perfect; >=90% when adaptation is possible or naturalistic cues exist; index rises with publication year r(64)=0.43; appearance vs surface-match instructions matter.
Cues: adaptation and local contrast (major), interreflection/shading, depth, specular highlights, memory colour; full adaptation takes several minutes.
Metamer mismatching (clothing in a badly lit store vs daylight) makes constancy impossible but is rare in natural scenes.
#TheDress pixels lie along the daylight locus; rotating them off-axis reduces individual differences; percept can be primed but not voluntarily changed.
Number of basic colour terms varies by language (11 English/German, 12 Russian, 15 Korean, 5 Himba/Berinmo); category effects are high-level and reduced by verbal interference.
practical_applications: Judge product colour in the plane lit directly but non-specularly; keep cue-rich scenes for true colour; fix green-magenta errors before warm-cool (derived).
limitations: Review; individual claims rest on cited studies not read here.

title: Color constancy
key_findings: Review of human colour constancy in Vision Research 51(7):674-700; excludes colour-vision deficiency and lightness constancy.
Author's site documents constancy indices (incl. Brunswik ratio) and a table of 80 indices from published studies.
practical_applications: Background for why constancy measurements vary with method (see WitzelGegenfurtner2018).
limitations: Full text not read; findings here only from search summaries and Witzel & Gegenfurtner's use of it.

title: Comprehensive color solutions: CAM16, CAT16, and CAM16-UCS
authors: Changjun Li, Zhiqiang Li, Zhifeng Wang, Yang Xu, Ming Ronnier Luo, Guihua Cui, Manuel Melgosa, Michael H. Brill, Michael Pointer
key_findings: CAM16 is a simpler revision of CIECAM02; CAT16 replaces CAT02 for chromatic adaptation alone; CAM16-UCS replaces CAM02-UCS for colour difference.
The 2016 conference version reports CAM16 solves the mathematical problems of CIECAM02 and performs as well or better.
Follow-up work (Gao et al. 2021) compensates the size effect in the CAT16 cone-like space.
practical_applications: Current appearance-model framework; supports the rule 'judge colour in final context and size'.
limitations: Abstract-level only; journal DOI not confirmed in this session; URL is the 2016 CIC conference version (A Revision of CIECAM02 and its CAT and UCS); follow-up only from search summary.

title: Perception of three-dimensional shape influences colour perception through mutual illumination
authors: Marina G. Bloj, Daniel Kersten, Anya C. Hurlbert
key_findings: Chromatic Mach card (magenta and white halves): the white side's perceived colour changes from pale pink to deep magenta when perceived shape flips concave/convex.
Visual system incorporates knowledge of mutual illumination early in colour processing.
practical_applications: Reflected colour (colour bleed) must be consistent with shape; cutouts need ground-colour bounce.
limitations: Abstract/summary level; PDF link returned 404.

title: Practical Pigment Mixing for Digital Painting
key_findings: RGB painting software mixes like light: blue + yellow -> grey instead of green.
Kubelka-Munk (1931) predicts pigment mixing (repeated absorption and scattering) but was never adopted by painting software.
Latent space: RGB as mixture of 4 primary pigments + additive residual, enabling K-M mixing with RGB in/out (Mixbox).
Plain subtractive mixing (as used by CMYK) gives results too dark or wrong in colour compared with K-M.
practical_applications: Do not fake paint overlaps with CSS blend; use AI-painted overlaps or a pigment mixer for watercolour styles.
limitations: Mixbox licence reported as CC BY-NC in secondary sources (not checked).

title: Ein Beitrag zur Optik der Farbanstriche
key_findings: Original two-flux model of light in paint layers (absorption K and scattering S), still widely used in industry.
practical_applications: Theoretical basis for pigment-mixing behaviour vs light mixing.
limitations: Not read; existence and page range from bibliographic records; English translation by S. Westin exists.

title: Color Compatibility From Large Datasets
authors: Peter O'Donovan, Aseem Agarwala, Aaron Hertzmann
key_findings: Analysed Kuler and COLOURLovers themes (>2 million created) and an MTurk rating set of 5-colour themes.
Little evidence that people gravitate to hue templates naturally or that matching a template gives higher scores; themes closely matching templates scored slightly lower.
Preference for hue entropy corresponding to about 2-3 hues per 5-colour theme.
Learned L1-regularised regression over features in several colour spaces predicts theme ratings; demographic groups rate differently.
practical_applications: Treat hue templates as idea generators; limit to 2-3 hue families; judge in context.
limitations: Context-free palettes rated online; interface bias in Kuler data acknowledged by authors.

title: Color Harmonization
authors: Daniel Cohen-Or, Olga Sorkine, Ran Gal, Tommer Leyvand, Ying-Qing Xu
key_findings: Finds the best-fitting harmonic hue template (8 types after Tokumaru et al. 2002 / Matsuda) and shifts image hues toward it with spatial coherence.
practical_applications: Tool for automatic palette unification of AI images; not evidence that templates are preferred.
limitations: Search summary only; PDF download failed in this session.

title: Additivity of colour harmony
authors: Li-Chen Ou, Patrick Chong, M. Ronnier Luo, Carl Minchew
key_findings: Harmony of a three-colour combination can be predicted by averaging the harmony of its three colour pairs (two-colour model).
Experiments in UK and US: 6545 three-colour wheels on a calibrated CRT and 111 interior images; simple and fairly robust predictor; may extend to more colours.
practical_applications: Check multi-colour palettes pair by pair, especially adjacent pairs.
limitations: Abstract only; lab and interior stimuli.

title: Colour harmony
authors: Stephen Westland, Kevin Laycock, Vien Cheung, Phil Henry, Forough Mahyar
key_findings: Review of major colour-harmony theories; asks whether fundamental laws of harmony exist; covers hue circularity, primaries and complementary colours.
practical_applications: Supports treating harmony schemes as conventions to test, not laws.
limitations: Search summary only.

title: Investigation of complementary colour harmony in CIELAB colour space
authors: Forough Mahyar, Vien Cheung, Stephen Westland, et al.
key_findings: AIC 2007 Midterm (Hangzhou) paper: opposite hues in CIELAB do not accurately predict perceived complementary relationships.
practical_applications: Do not treat 180-degree rotation in Lab/OKLCH as an exact complement.
limitations: Conference paper known only from a search summary; URL is the related review record.

title: Meta-Analysis of the Effect of Red on Perceived Attractiveness
authors: Gabrielle K. Lehmann, Andrew J. Elliot, Robert J. Calin-Jageman
key_findings: Adversarial collaboration (original proponent + replicators).
Publication-bias indicators significant for women (and for men without one outlier); effects decline with publication year.
Preregistered studies of women rating men: d=-0.10 vs 0.21 non-preregistered.
practical_applications: Never claim red 'makes' models or products more attractive.
limitations: Discussion section only partly read (page truncated).

title: Color and psychological functioning: a review of theoretical and empirical work
key_findings: Lists effects reported by >=5 labs (red before challenging tasks undermines performance; red in sport; red and attraction; blue light alertness; blue logos and trust appraisals).
Weaknesses: underpowered samples overestimate effects; colour rarely controlled at spectral level; theory either too specific or too general; focus on red.
Concludes it is 'premature to offer any bold theoretical statements, definitive empirical pronouncements'.
practical_applications: Use association language in briefs; avoid applied colour-psychology promises.
limitations: Pre-dates the 2018-2020 meta-analyses that weakened red effects.

title: Limited evidence for the effect of red color on cognitive performance: A meta-analysis
key_findings: 67 effect sizes, 38 samples, 22 publications (Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 27(6):1374-1382).
Anagram d=-0.06, knowledge d=-0.04 (n.s.); reasoning d=-0.34 [-0.61, -0.06].
Strong decline effect (early reasoning estimate ~-0.86) and publication bias; bias-adjusted effects near zero.
Casts doubt on a robust colour-priming effect in achievement situations.
practical_applications: Do not cite 'red impairs thinking/focus' in eye-care content.
limitations: Covers red and cognitive tests only.

title: Color Semantics in Human Cognition
key_findings: Colour-concept associations and colour meaning (semantics) are not the same and can conflict.

Color inference framework: pooling inference produces colour preferences (ecological valence; ~80% of variance in average US preferences); assignment inference maps colours to concepts considering the whole set.
Even abstract concepts have systematic colour associations; semantics is flexible and context dependent.
practical_applications: Choose legend/code colours so each concept's best match is distinct within the set; motif colours must not be reused for other meanings.
limitations: Mainly US/Western samples; visualisation context.

title: Color in Complex Scenes
authors: Steven K. Shevell, Frederick A. A. Kingdom
key_findings: In complex scenes an object's colour is not fully determined by the light from that object; chromatic representation also shapes texture, segmentation, depth, motion.
No variant of the equivalent-uniform-background hypothesis explains colour in complex scenes; chromatic variation in the surround alters perceived contrast (Brown & MacLeod 1997).

Cone signals cannot separate illuminant SPD from reflectance; gray-world and brightest-patch estimates miss cues such as specular reflections, shadows, mutual interreflections, luminance-chromaticity correlation.
Cites von Kries (1905) adaptation as classic baseline.
practical_applications: Busy colourful surrounds mute a product; cue-rich lighting supports true product colour.
limitations: Read in part (abstract, constancy section, figure notes).

title: Large shifts in color appearance from patterned chromatic backgrounds
key_findings: Two-chromaticity patterned backgrounds shift perceived colour more than a uniform background of either chromaticity.
Follow-ups explain shifts by S-cone spatially antagonistic receptive fields; assimilation and simultaneous contrast can act together.
practical_applications: Hatching over tints shifts the tint toward the line colour (assimilation).
limitations: Abstract and citing papers only.

title: Neural locus of color afterimages
authors: Qasim Zaidi, Robert Ennis, Dingcai Cao, Barry Lee
key_findings: Recordings from macaque retinal ganglion cells: afterimage signals originate in the retina (slow adaptation of RGC population) and may be modified by cortical processes.
practical_applications: Successive contrast between shots/slides is a low-level effect: preview sequences, not single stills.
limitations: Abstract via search; PMC page blocked by verification.

title: The Brightness of Colour
authors: David Corney, John-Dylan Haynes, Geraint Rees, R. Beau Lotto
key_findings: More saturated stimuli appear brighter at equal luminance (Helmholtz-Kohlrausch); blues and reds brighter than equiluminant yellows/greens, blue slightly more than red.
Bayesian ideal-observer model trained on natural surface statistics reproduces the effect; V1 fMRI responses track brightness, not luminance.
practical_applications: Eye overrates contrast of saturated red/blue text; always measure.
limitations: Effect sizes for humans described qualitatively; fMRI N=3; mechanism one proposal among several.

title: An Opponent-Process Theory of Color Vision
key_findings: Three opponent channels (red-green, blue-yellow, black-white) supported psychophysically with hue cancellation; helped reconcile Hering with trichromacy.
practical_applications: Conceptual basis for complementary afterimages and opponent contrast vocabulary.
limitations: Not read (PDF download failed); later work shows unique hues do not map neatly onto cone-opponent channels (search summary).

title: Computational Color Constancy: Survey and Experiments
authors: Arjan Gijsenij, Theo Gevers, Joost van de Weijer
key_findings: Taxonomy: static methods (gray-world, white-patch, gray-edge; unified in a Minkowski framework), gamut-based, learning-based.
Gray-world assumes the average scene reflectance under neutral light is achromatic; deviations are attributed to the illuminant.
Computational models cannot fully explain human constancy.
practical_applications: Explains why auto-WB fails in one-colour scenes (sea, foliage); shoot a neutral reference.
limitations: 2011 state of the art; deep-learning AWB since then not covered.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum) - WCAG 2.2
key_findings: 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text (>=18pt or >=14pt bold, ~24px / ~18.5px).
4.5:1 compensates contrast-sensitivity loss of about 20/40 acuity (typical around age 80).
Ratios are not rounded (4.499 fails); logotypes exempt but brand guidelines do not exempt ordinary text; background images with insufficient contrast fail.
practical_applications: Eyewear customers skew older: treat 4.5:1 as floor; measure text over photos on the worst patch.
limitations: Web-oriented; social images apply it by analogy. Year = WCAG 2.2 Recommendation year.

title: APCA in a Nutshell
key_findings: Lc 90 preferred body text; 75 minimum body text; 60 other content text; 45 headlines/large heavy text and detailed icons; 30 absolute minimum other text; 15 minimum non-text.
Developer describes APCA as candidate contrast method for WCAG 3; APCA Readability Criterion maintained separately, still in development.
practical_applications: Supplementary check for text on dark backgrounds.
limitations: Developer's own document; W3C draft says WCAG 3 contrast algorithm is yet to be determined (see W3C_WCAG3_WD).

title: Introduction to the ICC profile format (color.org profile page)
key_findings: An ICC profile provides data to convert between a device colour space and the device-independent PCS based on the CIE 1931 observer; PCS is 'virtual destination for input transforms and virtual source for output transforms'.
Four intents: media-relative colorimetric, ICC-absolute colorimetric (spot colours, proofing), saturation (vendor-specific, charts), perceptual (vendor-specific, photographs).
Current specification v4.4; iccMAX also exists.
practical_applications: Photos perceptual; brand colours relative colorimetric with proof; P3 -> sRGB conversion needs a deliberate intent.
limitations: Overview page, not the normative ICC.1 text.

title: ITU-R BT.709 entry, ICC characterization data registry (with BT.1886 notes)
key_findings: BT.709 defines a camera OETF (4.5L below 0.018, 0.45 power above), not a display EOTF; BT.1886 defines the display EOTF approx. power 2.4 deviating near black.
practical_applications: Export SDR clips as Rec.709; test on real phones because platforms interpret 709 differently.
limitations: Values from search summaries of the registry and secondary pages; ITU PDFs not opened.

title: Color space (MDN glossary) / Apple CGColorSpace displayP3
key_findings: Display P3 uses DCI-P3 primaries, D65 white point and the sRGB transfer function (original DCI-P3: ~6300K white, gamma 2.6).
Gamut about 25% larger than sRGB in area and ~50% in volume (secondary); CSS Color 4 predefines display-p3; color-gamut: p3 media query.
practical_applications: iPhone photos of saturated frames may clip when forced to sRGB; gamut-map deliberately.
limitations: Search summary of MDN/Apple/Wikipedia; Apple page fetch returned only the title.

title: Color Gamut Mapping
key_findings: Survey of 90+ gamut-mapping algorithms and ISO/CIE approaches; chapter on evaluating gamut-mapping algorithms.
Author chaired CIE TC 8-03 and helped create CIE guidelines for evaluating gamut-mapping algorithms.
practical_applications: Clip vs compress decision when moving P3 or sRGB content to print/smaller gamuts.
limitations: Publisher listing only.

title: Final Report of the O.S.A. Subcommittee on the Spacing of the Munsell Colors
authors: Sidney M. Newhall, Dorothy Nickerson, Deane B. Judd
key_findings: Describes a modified and enlarged Munsell solid from 1940 visual estimates (Munsell renotation), defined in the CIE (ICI) system under Illuminant C (JOSA 33(7):385-418).
practical_applications: Munsell H V/C vocabulary is tied to CIE colorimetry; usable in critique and convertible.
limitations: Abstract only; Munsell polar spacing cannot be perfectly uniform (secondary).

title: The Art of Pixar: The Complete Color Scripts and Select Art from 25 Years of Animation
key_findings: Collects the colour scripts of Pixar features; reviews/interviews credit Ralph Eggleston with starting colour scripts on Toy Story (small pastel drawings per scene focusing on basic colour).
Revised 2020 edition with foreword by Eggleston and introductions by Sharon Calahan and Harley Jessup.
practical_applications: Model for one-thumbnail-per-beat colour scripts.
limitations: Book not read; claims from publisher page, reviews and author interview summaries; dates of first colour script differ (1993 vs 1995).

title: Pixar in a Box - The Art of Lighting: Color scripts (Khan Academy)
key_findings: A colour script is a snapshot of the whole film with a frame painted from each scene, showing how each story moment will be lit and its overall colour and value structure (~7 min video).
Series also contains 'The Art of Lighting' and 'Learning Color Science from a Pixar Color Scientist'.
practical_applications: Basis for our per-beat colour-script template.
limitations: Khan Academy page failed to render in fetch; content from secondary listings.

title: If It's Purple, Someone's Gonna Die: The Power of Color in Visual Storytelling
key_findings: Practitioner book on colour in film storytelling (Focal Press).
practical_applications: Craft reference for motif colours; specific claims not usable until read.
limitations: Not read; bibliographic only.

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou? - cinematography by Roger Deakins (American Cinematographer)
key_findings: Shot in summer with lush greens; bleach-bypass/bi-pack tests could not desaturate selectively.

Deakins and Cinesite colorist Julius Friede selected the greens of trees/grass and turned them into 'dry browns and yellows' for the look of 'old, hand-tinted postcards'; little else changed; windows on only a couple of shots.
About 10 weeks in the digital suite; more manipulation added noise/artifacts.
practical_applications: Selective hue-range grading that protects skin; minimal secondaries on AI images.
limitations: Practitioner account; 'first DI' priority disputed (Pleasantville cited as earlier DI timing).

title: ACES documentation - background/overview
authors: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (ACES Central)
key_findings: Scene-referred framework; encodings ACES2065-1 (SMPTE ST 2065-1), ACEScg (linear AP1 for CG/compositing), ACEScct (log AP1 for grading).
Pipeline: input transform -> grading -> optional look -> rendering/output transform to display; ACES 1.3 added gamut compression (secondary).
practical_applications: Composite in linear light, grade, convert to display last.
limitations: Search summary of the docs and secondary guides.

title: CIE 224:2017 Colour Fidelity Index for accurate scientific use
key_findings: Defines general colour fidelity index Rf with 99 test colour samples and updated colour space; shares calculation framework with IES TM-30-18.
Rf is explicitly not a replacement for CRI Ra (CIE 13.3-1995) for product rating, specification or regulation.
practical_applications: Prefer lamps reported with Rf/TM-30 data for product photography and try-on mirrors.
limitations: Publisher page; full report paywalled.

title: TM-30: What have we learned in the past two years? (DOE presentation)
key_findings: TM-30-15: CAM02-UCS, 99 colour evaluation samples, Planckian/D-series reference; Rf, Rg, 16 Rcs,hj, 16 Rf,hj, colour vector graphic.

Summarising Royer et al. 2016 (Lighting Research & Technology): normalness and preference driven by red chroma + average fidelity; proposed criteria normalness Rf>=80 with 0%<=Rcs,h1<=8%; preference Rf>=74 with Rg>=100 or 0%<=Rcs,h16/h1<=15%.
practical_applications: Light specification for shop try-on and product photography.
limitations: Slide deck summarising peer-reviewed work; original LRT papers not read.

title: ISO/CIE 11664-2:2022 Colorimetry - Part 2: CIE standard illuminants
key_findings: D65 represents average daylight with CCT about 6500 K (6504 K exact after the c2 change); defined as a tabulated SPD, no recommended physical source.
practical_applications: D65 is the white of sRGB/BT.709/Display P3; 'daylight' lamps only approximate it.
limitations: Publisher page and secondary sources.

title: Billmeyer and Saltzman's Principles of Color Technology (3rd ed.) - definitions of metamerism
key_findings: Metamerism: different spectra with identical colorimetric coordinates for a single viewing condition; illuminant metamerism (match fails when light changes); observer metamerism (match fails for another observer).
practical_applications: Explains why frame parts/cases can match in the shop and differ in daylight.
limitations: Definitions quoted second-hand in a mailing-list post; book not read; 4th edition not checked.

title: Colors of the day in Thailand
authors: Wikipedia contributors (plus travel/culture pages in the same search)
key_findings: Sunday red, Monday yellow, Tuesday pink, Wednesday green, Thursday orange, Friday blue, Saturday purple; derived from Hindu astrology (navagraha), linked to Buddha images of the day; birth-day colour treated as lucky; royal ceremonies honour birthday colours.
Details vary between sources (Wednesday day/night).
practical_applications: Optional day-themed content; respect royal associations.
limitations: Tier E; not verified against Thai scholarly sources.

title: Thailand: One-year period of mourning declared
authors: Al Jazeera (and other news reports in the same search)
key_findings: After King Bhumibol's death (13 Oct 2016) the government declared one year of mourning; black and white worn nationwide; black clothing shortages; reports say other subdued colours were later accepted.
practical_applications: Use monochrome/black-white for condolence posts; pause festive palettes during national mourning.
limitations: News summaries; exact official wording not read.

title: Thai Color Terms and Their Structures
key_findings: Thai National Corpus (novels 2008-2017), 13 key colour words incl. separate 'blue' and 'light blue'; 332 non-basic colour terms found.

Applying Berlin & Kay strictly, concludes Thai is at stage 4 with 5 basic terms (white, black, red, yellow, green); blue, light blue, brown, purple, pink, orange, grey treated as non-basic because named after things.
practical_applications: Thai colour words in briefs carry object references; distinguish fa and nam-ngoen explicitly.
limitations: Corpus-linguistic, not perceptual; conclusion conflicts with other Thai studies (9-12 terms).

title: A comparison of Thai and Vietnamese color terms
key_findings: Reports 12 Thai basic colour terms (stage 7 of Berlin & Kay) and 9 Vietnamese.
practical_applications: Shows Thai basic-term count depends on criteria.
limitations: Search summary of repository record only; author's full name not confirmed.

title: Vision & Invention - chapter on colour discord (web edition)
key_findings: Discord = relational effect when a colour's value runs against its natural order (raised toward tint or lowered toward shade) next to another colour; types light, dark, double, muted discord.
Natural order: yellow lightest, violet darkest (after Rood/Carpenter); examples Bonnard, Vuillard, Impressionist light blue/violet shadows.
Use light discord sparingly to enliven; afterimages and simultaneous contrast strengthen discord.
practical_applications: Small value inversions for tension in story scenes.
limitations: Craft text; no empirical support.

title: Okhsv and Okhsl - two new color spaces for color picking
key_findings: HSL lightness 'does not match the perception of lightness well at all for saturated colors'; HSV hue has severe distortions; both built on sRGB without appearance research and not continuously differentiable.
Okhsv/Okhsl keep OKLab hue with cylindrical sRGB mapping; goals (perceptual L/h, cylinder, smooth variation) conflict; sRGB only.
practical_applications: Use Okhsl-style pickers or OKLCH, never HSL S/L to judge equal lightness/vividness.
limitations: Author's blog, not peer-reviewed; publication date not confirmed on page.
license: unknown (blog; code MIT per author, not checked)
